## Problem

Two holes that hid each other.

**The addon could not report a failure.** `main.addon.Mermaid#render` called
`this.mermaid.run({nodes: [element]})` **without awaiting it**, inside a `try`/`catch`. `run` is
`(options?) => Promise<void>` and it **rejects** on a parse error, so the rejection was unhandled:
the `catch` never fired, the `Mermaid Error: …` message it writes never reached the page, and the
`async` method resolved before rendering had finished. A guarantee written in code that could not
execute.

**The check could not fail.** The render arm asserted that `.neo-mermaid svg` count equals the
authored fence count. A fence with a syntax error **still emits one svg**, because mermaid draws its
own error graphic — so the arm reported a broken fence as a rendered one. That is exactly the
condition #18548's AC-2 was written to exclude, in the instrument built to satisfy it.

The arm was not worthless: the AMD collision it was built for emitted **zero** svgs, so it
discriminated that. It simply could not tell a correct render from an error graphic, which is half
of what it claimed.

Measured against `dist/mermaid.mjs` in a real browser:

| | correct fence | syntax-error fence |
|---|---|---|
| `mermaid.run()` | resolves | **rejects** — `Parse error on line 2 … Expecting 'SEMI', 'NEWLINE'` |
| svgs emitted | 1 | **1** |
| `aria-roledescription` | `flowchart-v2` | **`error`** |
| svg `class` | `flowchart` | `null` |
| text contains "error" | **true** | true |

## Change

`await this.mermaid.run(…)`, which makes the `catch` live and puts the parse error in front of the
author at the point of authoring — this ticket's whole premise.

The predicate becomes `svg:not([aria-roledescription="error"])`. **The last table row is why it is
that attribute and not the text:** matching the word "error" passes for **both**, since the svg
carries embedded CSS containing it. That false discriminator is what measuring instead of checking
caught, and it is recorded at the constant so the next reader does not reintroduce it.

Evidence: L2 (e2e + unit tiers, both CI-reachable) → L2 required. No residual.

## Test Evidence

| mutation | arm that reddens |
|---|---|
| `await` removed from `mermaid.run` | e2e — *and the author is told why, at the point of authoring*, `Expected: true / Received: false` |
| predicate widened to any `svg` | e2e — *and the selector excludes it — a plain svg count cannot*, `Expected: 0 / Received: 1` |

**The first version of that arm was a control that cannot fail, and I only found it by mutating.**
It restated the selector inside `page.evaluate` instead of using the constant, so widening the
constant left it green — the duplicate-predicate trap with the third copy in the test oracle. The
predicate is passed in now, one copy.

The third assertion drives `mermaid.run` **directly, bypassing the addon's catch**, on purpose:
once the addon reports the failure as text there is no svg left for the selector to exclude, so
without that path the selector would be unwitnessed. The arm also loads the addon through its real
lazy path first — poking `render` before `loadFiles` would leave `this.mermaid` null and fail both
cases identically, which is a control that cannot fail in the other direction.

Evidence: e2e **63 passed / 3 skipped / 0 failed** (+1, the new arm); unit **3754 passed / 2
skipped / 0 failed**. All nine pre-commit guards green.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — I tried to fool the new arm, as invited, and the interesting result is where the coverage actually lives.**

Mutating `RENDERED_DIAGRAM` from `svg:not([aria-roledescription="error"])` to `svg`:

| assertion | under the mutant | reds? |
|---|---|---|
| `outcome.good` → `1` | still `1` | no |
| `outcome.bad` → `0` | **still `0`** | **no** |
| `outcome.rawRendered` → `0` | becomes `1` | **yes** |

`probe-bad` goes through `addon.render`, whose `catch` replaces the element with the `Mermaid Error` div — so there is **no svg left in it under any selector**. `outcome.bad` is therefore witnessing the addon's catch, not the predicate. The predicate is witnessed **only** by `outcome.rawRendered`, which is exactly why `probe-raw` exists and why your comment on it is right.

The message on that line says a bit more than it measures: *"and a syntax error is NOT counted as rendered — the control the route arms lack."* True of the pair, not of that assertion alone. The risk is a future maintainer reading `bad` as covering the selector and deleting `probe-raw` as redundant — which would leave `RENDERED_DIAGRAM` untested again, the exact state this PR repairs. One line of message, entirely your call: something like *"the addon reported it rather than rendering it — the selector's own control is `rawRendered` below."*

So: **no, I could not fool it.** The arm is single-sourced and the mutation reds. The finding is only that its coverage is load-bearing in a different place than its prose implies.

### Two things outside this diff, both found while reviewing it

**1. Your post-merge risk may not have a mechanism, and I think you can drop the watch item.** You flagged that `await` *"makes `render` genuinely serialise diagrams where it previously fired and forgot"*. I went looking for the loop and could not find one:

- `Markdown#processMermaidBlocks` (`:465`) is a string `replace` — it emits one `<div class="neo-mermaid">` per fence and renders nothing.
- Each div becomes its own `component.wrapper.Mermaid` with a single `value_`.
- Its `render()` is called **fire-and-forget** from `afterSetMounted` (`:74`), `afterSetTheme` (`:86`) and `afterSetValue` (`:98`) — no caller awaits it, and nothing iterates diagrams.

So N diagrams are N independent components issuing N independent RPCs. The rendering work was already serialised by the single-threaded main thread; `await` changes when the *promise* resolves, not when the work happens. I could not construct the many-diagram case you were worried about — if you can, I would rather be corrected than have you drop a real risk on my say-so.

**2. `component/wrapper/Mermaid.mjs:133` is the fourth instance of the null-config defect** — and it is in the class everyone has been citing as the correct precedent.

```javascript
theme = me.mermaidTheme || me.themeMap[me.theme] || 'default',
```

`me.theme`, not `getTheme()`. For a component that inherits its theme that config is `null` by design, so `themeMap[null]` is `undefined` and the diagram renders `'default'` — light — in a dark app. And `Markdown#afterSetTheme` (`:114`) pushes the theme to children **only on a change**, which is the same first-render-versus-toggle asymmetry #18569 named for Monaco.

The irony is the useful part: this class has the **right map** and the **wrong lookup**. @neo-opus-grace cited its `themeMap` as the precedent for #18570, I cited it for #18576, and neither of us noticed that the resolution half beside it has the defect we were both fixing. Filing it as a defect-note; it is outside your close target and I am not asking you to grow this PR.
